LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only parses the PKGBUILD file to extract its metadata (function definitions, variable assignments, source arrays, etc.). During this phase, no top-level executable code is executed—only the file is read and analyzed structurally. 

There is no command substitution, no shell invocation, and no code that runs outside of the standard build pipeline functions (`pkgver()`, `build()`, `package()`). While the source array includes a local file reference (`file://Plants_vs._Zombies_1.2.0.1073_EN.zip`), this is merely a source specification and does not cause any execution during `--printsrcinfo`. The checksum is marked as `SKIP`, which is explicitly permitted by the guidelines and does not constitute a security issue for this gate.

All function definitions are present but not invoked at the top level, meaning they remain dormant until the full build process begins. Since no malicious or unintended code is present that would execute during the metadata extraction phase, the command is safe to run.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The PKGBUILD contains only declarative metadata (source array, checksums, function definitions) without any executable top-level code. `makepkg --printsrcinfo` safely parses the file structure without executing any commands.</summary>
